summary: Many customers get strong value from the travel credit, lounges, insurance, points boost and transfer partners, often more than the annual fee. The most common complaints are credits that are hard to use (DoorDash, The Edit, StubHub), poor support when portal bookings go wrong, crowded lounges, and a higher fee after the refresh.

Many customers say it changed how they handle money, with zero-based budgeting that is worth the subscription once learned. The main complaint is price increases, and quite a few moved to Actual Budget or spreadsheets. Others cite manual entry, a learning curve, bank sync gaps, and interface changes.

Customers who travel or live in cities say the lounges, Fine Hotels stays and credits (Uber, Resy, airline, Lululemon) outweigh the high annual fee. Others call it a coupon book that is hard to use and poor for everyday earning. Lounge crowding and recent hotel credit changes bothered some.

Most customers rate the customer service highly and like having investing, cash and retirement accounts in one place, with the cash sweep earning interest. Many prefer it to Vanguard and Schwab. A sizable minority report transfers or deposits held for weeks, account locks, and a glitchy app.

Customers like the interface, reporting and Mint-style overview, and many moved from Mint, YNAB or Copilot. The most common complaints are accounts that stop syncing and slow support, plus higher pricing and budgeting that some find less hands-on than YNAB. Experience depends on the banks connected.

Many customers like it for travel, currency exchange, transfers and the app, and some use it as a main bank for years. The dominant complaint is support: accounts frozen, blocked or closed with little explanation, slow appeals and chat bots. Outages and fee changes also came up, so some keep another bank as backup.

Customers like earning points on rent with no annual fee, plus the transfer partners and travel perks. Many are unhappy with the 2.0 changes, which they say cut benefits and made earning more complicated. Support experiences are mixed, with several fraud cases handled well and others slowly.

Most customers use it for international transfers and like the low, upfront fees, good exchange rates and reliability, including for large sums. The main complaints are accounts blocked or transfers held, cancelled or delayed during reviews, with support hard to reach. A few found bank wires cheaper for very large amounts.

Most customers are long-time customers who like the app, buckets, lack of fees and ATM fee reimbursement, and many praise the customer service. Some report accounts locked or frozen with slow, frustrating support. A few found rates lower than competitors or missed having cash deposits and branches.

Most customers describe a simple high-yield savings account with quick transfers, no fees and no problems for years. The main complaint is accounts locked or withdrawals blocked after security or identity reviews, with frustrating phone support. Some also mention rates falling and the lack of a mobile app.

Most customers who eat out and buy groceries a lot are happy with the 4x earning and points value. The annual fee is the main sticking point, and the dining and delivery credits (Dunkin, Grubhub, Resy) are easy for city dwellers but awkward elsewhere. Some cancel or keep it only after retention offers.

Customers mostly love the high cash back on dining, entertainment, groceries and streaming, and it is often a most-used card, sometimes paired with the Venture X. The annual fee is worth it for heavy dining and entertainment spenders but not for everyone. A few report accounts closed or restricted without explanation.

Customers who like it praise the clean, fast interface, quick transaction syncing and good recurring and investment views. Complaints are slow development, thin reports and budgeting, and the lack of a web or Android app. Some left for Monarch or YNAB, while others stay because of the design.

Customers mostly find it easy to justify, as the travel credit and anniversary miles offset the annual fee, and they value the lounge access, simple 2x earning and portal pricing. Downsides are a portal-only travel credit that some find cumbersome and recent lounge access changes that hurt solo travelers and those with guests.

Customers value the Hyatt and airline transfer partners, primary rental car coverage and no foreign transaction fees, with the points often worth it for travel. The main frustrations are a portal hotel credit that is hard to use, reduced redemption value, and the annual fee. Support experiences are mixed.

Most customers like the clean app, daily cash back, extra cash back on Apple Pay and no foreign transaction fees, and many use it mainly for interest-free Apple device financing. The physical card earns less, and some find it thin on benefits. Fraud and dispute handling through Goldman Sachs frustrated a number of customers.

Most customers use it as a simple flat-rate catch-all and keep it for years, with easy redemption and handy price protections. The main complaint is Citi customer service, especially fraud flags and disputes ruled for the merchant. Some also dislike benefits being cut, the shift to ThankYou points, and the foreign transaction fee.

Customers mostly like it as a simple flat-rate catch-all with a solid sign-up bonus, no annual fee and cell phone protection. Product changes from other Wells Fargo cards were easy. Complaints include redemption rules, such as increments and the removed check option, low credit limits and weaker customer service for some.

Most customers use it as an everyday catch-all, earning a flat rate plus bonus rewards on dining and drugstores, often alongside a Sapphire card. Product changes and in-branch offers usually went smoothly. Some say it feels less competitive now, and a few had promotions or bonus credits not honored or missing.

Customers mostly like the rotating bonus categories, the dining and drugstore bonus, and stacking offers such as PayPal quarters for much higher returns. Some find the categories a hassle to track or unhelpful in certain quarters. A few had trouble getting welcome bonuses honored. Phone protection claims were generally easy.

Most customers got the deposit back and moved to an unsecured card within roughly half a year to a year, often with generous limit increases, and praise the phone support. A few hit account verification demands, long delays or closures, and one never graduated after two years.

Fans say the card's credits, airline rebate and lounge access make it worth keeping, especially for people who travel or spend a lot on it. The annual fee is the recurring complaint, and several cancelled after perks were cut or found the points poor. Retention help and support experiences are mixed.

Customers' opinion is split. Some customers find it fast, consistent and good value for everyday transaction tracking, while others call it buggy, with unreliable account connections, wrong or missing transactions, and weak investment tracking. Several left for Monarch over limited budgeting methods and no rollover support.

Most customers use it as a dependable main checking account for years, citing free ATM withdrawals, decent interest and good customer service. The recurring downsides are slow bill pay and incoming transfers, no Zelle, and occasional website or linking glitches. One had it briefly frozen by fraud checks.

Customers who want a simple zero-based monthly budget like it, often using the free version with manual entry, and some chose it over YNAB for being less complex. Critics find it clunky and say sinking funds were unreliable. Bank sync is not part of the free tier.

Tiller pulls bank and card transactions into Google Sheets or Excel, and spreadsheet fans love the flexibility and shared templates. Customers say it is not for everyone: it is less structured and not user friendly for beginners, some find it too manual, and connections need occasional refreshing.

Customers praise the high cash back on groceries and streaming, saying it easily covers the annual fee. Some note a spending cap on groceries and use a backup card past it. Support and the app were called good, and no real complaints came up.

Customers like it as a long-term main card, with easy rotating bonus categories that many activate and max out each quarter. Customer service reaches a person quickly, and the first-year match and intro APR approvals impressed some. No real downsides came up.

Users value TurboTax Online for convenience, since it imports forms from banks and brokerages and handles quirky returns. The main complaint is fees: many were pushed into paid tiers late in the process or hit an unclear extra charge for paying from the refund, and several left for free alternatives. A few got through free for years.

Users, most of them switching from TurboTax, describe FreeTaxUSA as easy, cheap and accurate, with federal filing free and only a small state fee. It handles self-employment, rentals and investments well for many, without the constant upsells. A few missed direct imports, struggled with large stock-trade lists, or had a special situation handled wrongly.

Users mostly treat Rocket Money as a stand-in after Mint or Monarch, finding it fairly good though not quite as polished as Monarch. A few had trouble connecting some banks, cards or a mortgage account.
